subject: Christian Religious Studies
examFormat: The aim of the UTME syllabus in Christian Religious Studies is to prepare candidates for the Board’s examination and to test their achievement of the course objectives: to acquire knowledge and understanding of the tenets of the Christian faith as contained in the Bible, to interpret biblical teachings and themes, to apply biblical teachings and tenets to life in society, and to evaluate the level of that application. The syllabus has four sections: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom; Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets; Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles; and Themes from selected Epistles. It states no exam format.

Christian Religious Knowledge for Secondary Schools, Books 1-3 — I. O. Adeyemo et al (Ibadan: Onibonoje, 1998)
Christian Religious Knowledge for Senior Secondary Schools, Books 1-3 — A. A. Adeyinka et al (Lagos: Longman, 1991)
Christian Religious Knowledge for Senior Secondary Schools — H. A. Adigwe et al (Onitsha: Africana Publishers, 2004)
Senior Secondary School Christian Religious Knowledge: Themes from Selected Epistles, Vols. I-III — E. O. N. Aghaeghuna (Awka: Jet Publishers, 1988)
Christian Religious Knowledge for Senior Secondary Schools, Books 1-3 — A. Dopamu et al (Lagos: Nelson, 1990)
Christian Religious Knowledge for Senior Secondary Schools, Books 1-3 — J. A. Ilori et al (Ibadan: Evans, 1980)

topics.name: The Sovereignty of God
objectives: define the term ‘sovereignty’
analyse God’s process of creation
interpret the sequence of creation
identify man’s role in advancing God’s purpose in creation
topics.content: God as Creator and Controller of the Universe (Gen. 1 and 2); cf. Amos 9:5-6; Is. 45:5-12; Ps. 19:1-6; Jer. 18:1-16; Rom. 8:28.

topics.name: The Covenant
objectives: explain the concept of covenant
examine the importance and implication of the covenants
distinguish between God’s covenants with Noah, Abraham and Israel
distinguish between the old and the new covenants

subtopics.name: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)

topics.name: Leadership Qualities
objectives: examine the circumstances that gave rise to the leadership of Joseph, Moses, Joshua and the Judges
identify the major talents of these leaders
assess God’s role in the works of these leaders
analyse the achievements of these leaders
topics.content: Examples of leaders: Joseph, Moses, Joshua and the Judges.

topics.name: Divine Providence, Guidance and Protection
objectives: identify the different ways by which God guided and protected the people of Israel
specify how God provided for His people
identify the different occasions when God provided for Israel

topics.name: Parental Responsibility
objectives: determine the extent to which Eli, Samuel and David were responsible for the short-comings of their children
describe how Asa pleased God

topics.name: Obedience and Disobedience
objectives: determine why Abraham, the three Hebrew youths and David obeyed God
identify the rewards for obedience
compare the disobedience of Adam, the people of Israel, Moses and Saul
indicate the reasons for their disobedience
identify the consequences of disobedience
topics.content: Disobedience and Consequences: Adam (Gen. 2:15-25; 3), collection of manna (Ex. 16:22-30), the golden calf (Ex. 32), Moses (Num. 20:7-12; Deut. 34:1-6), Saul (1 Sam. 10:1-16; 15:1-25; 16:14-23; 31:1-13).

subtopics.name: Obedience and Rewards: Abraham (Gen. 22:1-19), the three Hebrew youths (Dan. 3:1-30), David (1 Sam. 30:1-20)

topics.name: A Man After God’s Own Heart
objectives: identify David’s anointing experience
specify how David submitted to the will of God
examine the situations that led to David’s sin and repentance
identify why God forgave David

subtopics.name: David’s submission to the will of God (1 Sam. 26:1-25; 2 Sam. 12:15-25)
David’s repentance and forgiveness (2 Sam. 11; 12:1-15; cf. Ps. 51:1-30)

topics.name: Decision-Making
objectives: identify the source of Solomon’s wisdom
compare the different ways used by Saul and Solomon in making decisions
analyse the decisions made by Saul, Solomon and Rehoboam
assess the consequences of Solomon and Rehoboam’s unwise decisions

subtopics.name: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)

topics.name: Greed and its Effects
objectives: deduce the meaning of greed
distinguish between Ahab and Gehazi’s greed
analyse the consequences of Ahab and Gehazi’s greed

topics.name: The Supremacy of God
objectives: assess the religious situation in Israel at the time of Elijah and Ahab
identify the characters involved in the contest on Mount Carmel
differentiate between God’s power and that of Baal
topics.content: Religious tension and the power of God on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 16:29-34; 17:1-7; 18; 19:1-18).

topics.name: Religious Reforms in Judah
objectives: analyse Josiah’s religious reforms
determine the reasons for the renewal of the covenant
assess the significance of the reforms

topics.name: Concern for Judah
objectives: identify the reasons for the fall of Jerusalem
examine the condition of Judah during the exile
analyse the people’s response to the call of Nehemiah and Ezra to rebuild Jerusalem
distinguish between Nehemiah and Ezra’s responses to the opposition of their enemies

subtopics.name: Response to the state of Judah (Neh. 2; 4:1-23; Ezra 3:4; 5; 6; 7)

topics.name: Faith, Courage and Protection
objectives: analyse the stories of Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego and Daniel
determine the occasions in which the four men demonstrated faith
analyse the effects of the faith of the four men on the Babylonians
topics.content: Examples of Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego (Dan. 3:1-30; 6:1-28).

topics.name: God’s Message to Nineveh
objectives: analyse the story of Jonah’s call
describe the consequences of Jonah’s disobedience
assess the effect of Jonah’s message on the Ninevites
emulate the example of the Ninevites

topics.name: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
objectives: determine what true religion is
identify the ills that led to the call for social justice in Amos’ time
examine the condition in Israel during Hosea’s time
analyse Hosea’s portrayal of divine love and human response

subtopics.name: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)

topics.name: Holiness and Divine Call
objectives: distinguish the calls of Isaiah, Ezekiel and Jeremiah
compare the assignments given to these prophets
determine the need for God’s people to be holy

topics.name: Punishment and Hope
objectives: describe the situations that led to the punishment of Israel
identify the conditions for hope
determine the benefits of restoration

topics.name: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
objectives: compare the stories of the births of John and Jesus
assess the importance of John as the forerunner of Jesus
describe the boyhood of Jesus

subtopics.name: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)

topics.name: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
objectives: determine the meaning and purpose of the baptism of Jesus
enumerate the temptations of Jesus
examine the significance of the temptations of Jesus

topics.name: Discipleship
objectives: identify the first disciples to be called by Jesus
determine the demands of discipleship

subtopics.name: The call of the first disciples (Mt. 4:18-22; 9:9-13; Mk. 1:16-20; 2:13-17; Lk. 5:1-11, 27-32)

topics.name: Miracles
objectives: classify the different miracles of Jesus
indicate the occasion of each of the miracles
examine the significance of each of the miracles
topics.content: Nature miracles: stilling the storm (Mt. 8:23-27; Mk. 4:35-41; Lk. 8:22-25), feeding of the five thousand (Mt. 14:13-24; Mk. 6:30-44; Lk. 9:10-17; Jn. 6:1-13), walking on the sea (Mt. 14:22-26; Mk. 6:45-52; Jn. 6:16-21), changing water to wine (Jn. 2:1-11). Miracles of resuscitation: the raising of Lazarus (Jn. 11:1-45), Jairus’ daughter (Lk. 8:41-42, 49-56; Mk. 5:21-43), the widow’s son at Nain (Lk. 7:11-17). Healing miracles: the lepers (Mt. 8:1-4; Mk. 1:40-45; Lk. 5:12-16; 17:11-19), the paralytic at the pool (Jn. 5:1-17), the centurion’s servant (Mt. 8:5-13; Lk. 7:1-10), the blind (Jn. 9:1-12; Mk. 10:46-52; Lk. 18:35-43). Exorcism: the Gerasene (Gadarene) demoniac (Mt. 8:28-34; Mk. 5:1-20; Lk. 8:26-39), the epileptic boy (Mk. 9:14-29; Lk. 9:37-43; Mt. 17:14-21).

topics.name: The Parables
objectives: classify the different parables of Jesus
identify the occasion of each parable
interpret the meaning of each parable
give reasons why Jesus taught in parables
topics.content: Parables of the kingdom: the sower (Mt. 13:1-23; Mk. 4:1-20), the weeds (Mt. 13:24-30, 36-43), the drag-net (Mt. 13:47-50), the wedding garment (Mt. 22:1-14).

subtopics.name: Parables about love of God (Mt. 18:12-14; Lk. 15:1-32)
Parables about love for one another (Lk. 10:25-37; 16:19-31)
Parable about wealth: the rich fool (Lk. 12:13-21)

topics.name: Sermon on the Mount
objectives: analyse the teachings on the Mount
identify the demands of the Kingdom
determine the consequences of placing worldly possessions above heavenly treasures
associate the rewards for obedience with the sermon on the Mount

topics.name: Mission of the Disciples
objectives: distinguish between the mission of the twelve and the seventy
specify the instructions to the disciples
assess the outcomes of the missions

subtopics.name: The mission of the twelve (Mt. 10:5-15; Mk. 6:7-13; Lk. 9:1-16)

topics.name: The Great Confession
objectives: analyse the confession by Peter
identify the occasion of the Great Confession
examine the significance of the Great Confession

topics.name: The Transfiguration
objectives: trace the events leading to the Transfiguration
determine the significance of the Transfiguration to the disciples
identify the personalities involved in the Transfiguration account

topics.name: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
objectives: recount the Triumphal Entry and the cleansing of the Temple
determine the significance of the Triumphal Entry and the cleansing of the Temple
examine how the cleansing of the Temple caused hostility towards Jesus

topics.name: The Last Supper
objectives: trace the story of the Last Supper
evaluate the significance of the Last Supper

topics.name: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
objectives: analyse the different trials of Jesus
describe the crucifixion and burial of Jesus
deduce the lessons of the death of Jesus

subtopics.name: The trial of Jesus before the High Priest (Mt. 26:36-75; Mk. 14:53-72; Lk. 22:66-71)
The trial of Jesus before Pilate (Mt. 27:11-26; Mk. 15:1-15; Lk. 23:1-5, 13-25; Jn. 18:28-40; 19:1-16)
The trial of Jesus before Herod (Lk. 23:6-12)
Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)

topics.name: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
objectives: trace the stories of the resurrection, appearances and ascension of Jesus
compare the personalities involved in the stories
analyse the relevance of the resurrection and ascension of Jesus

topics.name: Jesus’ Teachings about Himself
objectives: analyse the different teachings of Jesus about Himself
deduce the reasons for Jesus’ teachings about Himself
interpret the meanings of the symbols used by Jesus about Himself

subtopics.name: The Bread of Life and the Living Water (Jn. 4:7-15; 6:25-58)
The Door, the Lamb and the Good Shepherd (Jn. 1:29-34; 10:1-18)

topics.name: Love
objectives: describe God’s love for man
specify the ways they can love one another
evaluate the significance of love

subtopics.name: Love for one another (Jn. 13:34-35; 15:12-13; cf. 1 Jn. 4:7-21; 1 Cor. 13)

topics.name: Fellowship in the Early Church
objectives: identify the reasons for communal living in the Early Church
identify the problems of communal living and their solutions
examine how communal living helped the growth of the Early Church

subtopics.name: Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11; 6:1-6)

topics.name: The Holy Spirit and the Mission of the Church
objectives: trace the story of the Pentecost
examine the significance of the Pentecost experience
analyse the mission of the Church

topics.name: Opposition to the Gospel Message
objectives: trace the story of the arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John
trace the events that led to the martyrdom of Stephen
describe the role of Saul in the persecution of the Church
evaluate the importance of persecution to the growth of the Church
account for the persecution of Paul

subtopics.name: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)

topics.name: Mission to the Gentiles
objectives: compare the conversions of Saul and Cornelius
analyse the commissioning and mission of Paul
examine the main decisions at the Council of Jerusalem
identify the personalities involved at the Council of Jerusalem
examine the relevance of the main decisions at the Council of Jerusalem
assess Paul’s role in the mission to the Gentiles

subtopics.name: The commissioning and mission of Paul (Acts 13; 14:1-20)

topics.name: Justification by Faith
objectives: interpret the phrase ‘justification by faith’
identify the basic conditions for justification
determine the fruits of justification

topics.name: The Law and Grace
objectives: examine the purpose and significance of the law and grace
identify the place of the Law among the Jews

topics.name: New Life in Christ
objectives: describe the characteristics of the old life
analyse the new life in Christ
identify the conditions of the new life
examine the benefits of the new life

topics.name: Christians as Joint Heirs with Christ
objectives: describe how Christians are joint heirs with Christ
indicate the benefits of being joint heirs with Christ

topics.name: Humility
objectives: determine the meaning of humility
identify the requirements of humility
identify the rewards of humility

topics.name: Forgiveness
objectives: analyse Paul’s teaching on forgiveness
assess the benefits of forgiveness

topics.name: Spiritual Gifts
objectives: identify the different spiritual gifts
analyse the benefits of spiritual gifts to the individual and the church

topics.name: Christian Giving
objectives: interpret the concept of Christian giving
relate the teachings of Paul on Christian giving
identify the importance of Christian giving

topics.name: Civic Responsibility
objectives: identify the need for obedience to authority
specify the requirements of good citizenship

topics.name: Dignity of Labour
objectives: interpret the concept of dignity of labour
analyse the benefits of labour

topics.name: The Second Coming of Christ
objectives: identify the signs of the Second Coming of Christ
specify the preparations for His coming
indicate what will happen during His Second Coming
examine the importance of His coming

subtopics.name: The signs of the Coming of Christ (1 Thess. 4:13-18; 2 Thess. 2:1-12)
Preparation for His coming (1 Thess. 5:1-11; 2 Pet. 3:1-13; Matt. 25:31-46)

topics.name: Impartiality
objectives: interpret the concept of impartiality
identify causes of partiality
examine the consequences of partiality

topics.name: Effective Prayer
objectives: identify the requirements of effective prayer
distinguish between effective and ineffective prayer
identify the importance of prayer

topics.name: Christian Living in the Community
objectives: determine interpersonal relationships among Christians
analyse Christian living among non-Christians
relate Christian attitude to persecution
determine the relationship in the Christian family
examine the importance of maintaining good relationships

subtopics.name: Interpersonal relationships among Christians (1 Pet. 5:1-4; Rom. 12:3-21; 2 Pet. 1:3-11; Heb. 13:1-21)
Christians living among non-Christians (1 Pet. 2:3-25; Rom. 15:1-2)
Relationship in the Christian family (Eph. 6:1-9; Col. 3:18-21; 1 Pet. 3:1-7)

topics.name: Corruption
objectives: define the term corruption
identify the causes of corruption
determine the effects and consequences of corruption
identify ways of curbing corruption

topics.name: Sexual Immorality
objectives: identify what constitute sexual immorality
determine the causes of sexual immorality
examine the effects and consequences of sexual immorality
identify ways of curbing sexual immorality

subtopics.name: Adultery and Fornication (Heb. 13:4; Eph. 5:3-10; cf. Matt. 5:28-32; Deut. 22:22; Lev. 20:10)
